questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The angle of friction θ is related to the coefficient of limiting friction μ as:
questions.explanation: The angle of friction is the angle between the resultant of friction and normal reaction and the normal reaction itself, giving tan θ = f/N = μ.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Lenz's law, which fixes the direction of the induced current, is a direct consequence of the conservation of:
questions.explanation: The induced current opposes the change producing it, so work must be done against this opposition, which is exactly conservation of energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The binding energy of a nucleus is related to its mass defect Δm by:
questions.explanation: The mass of a nucleus is less than the sum of its nucleons, and this mass defect appears as binding energy through E = Δm c².

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of unpaired electrons present in a ground state nitrogen atom (Z = 7) is:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is 1s² 2s² 2p³. By Hund's rule the three 2p electrons occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins, so three electrons are unpaired.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 2: Structure of Atom

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which colligative property is most suitable for determining the molecular mass of polymers and proteins?
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure is measurable even in very dilute solutions and is determined at room temperature, which avoids damaging heat-sensitive biomolecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Addition of HBr to propene in the absence of peroxide gives mainly:
questions.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule hydrogen adds to the carbon carrying more hydrogens, so bromine goes to C-2 through the more stable secondary carbocation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Euglena is often described as a connecting link between plants and animals because it:
options: Has a rigid cellulose cell wall
Has chlorophyll but is heterotrophic in the dark
questions.explanation: Euglenoids are photosynthetic in sunlight but behave as heterotrophs in the dark, and they have a protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In any ecosystem, the pyramid of energy is always:
questions.explanation: Energy is lost as heat at every transfer, so each higher trophic level holds less energy. Pyramids of number and biomass can be inverted, but energy never is.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A person with blood group AB can receive blood from which group or groups?
questions.explanation: Group AB plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so it is the universal recipient, while group O is the universal donor.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Industrial melanism observed in the peppered moth in England is a classic example of:
questions.explanation: After industrialisation soot-darkened tree trunks hid the dark moths from predators, so their frequency rose. This is directional natural selection.
